newsitem.title: INDIA: Soybean-India seen increasing crop area.
newsitem.headline: Soybean-India seen increasing crop area.

text.p: India is expected to step up area under soybean cultivation to 5.7 million hectares in the 1997/98 season (November/October) from 5.0 million in the current year, a trade organisation said on Tuesday.

The Soybean Processors' Association of India (SOPA), based at Indore, said farmers in India's central state of Madhya Pradesh, the country's soybean bowl, had geared up for sowing with the arrival of pre-monsoon rains.
Regular rains are expected in the next few days.
SOPA cautioned farmers to sow soybean only after their lands received a rainfall of 7.0-8.0 cm.
"The soil should have enough moisture for good seed germination," a SOPA official said. Pre-monsoon rains had so far brought in a rainfall of about 4.0 cm.
SOPA has set a soybean production target of 5.7 million tonnes for the country and 4.0 million for Madhya Pradesh in the 1997/98 season.
SOPA expects the area under soybean in Madhya Pradesh to increase to 4.0 million hectares in 1997/98 from 3.7 million hectares in the current season.
It has estimated that nearly 700,000 tonnes of soybean stock is with the farmers, of which 500,000 tonnes are meant for sowing and the remainder for re-sowing if need be.
Arrivals of soybean in central Indian markets have dwindled to around 1,000 tonnes compared to 1,500 tonnes at the same time a year ago.
Soybean was quoted around 12,000/12,900 rupees per tonne, just about the same price prevailed last year.
Traders said soymeal prices, however, were higher this year at $305/306 per tonne compared to $268/270 per tonne in the same month last year.
According to trade sources, India has so far exported 2.3 million tonnes of soymeal in the 1996/97 season against a total export of 2.6 million in the previous year.
Traders said soymeal production had sharply come down because of poor arrivals.
They said the crushing capacity utilisation in local soymeal processing units had come down to 8.0/10 percent in the current season against 12/14 percent last year.
